evidence.V1: Top view reads clearly as an L corner and the front/three-quarter read as masonry, but the 3/4 silhouette is a plain slab with tiny course notches - the corner is not identifiable from outline alone.
evidence.V2: Big L mass, medium courses with quoin pairs, plinth and cap; no small-scale detail beyond the chamfers, so hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Chunky chamfered blocks fit the kit but the layout is a stiff rectangular grid; quoins alternate one wide / two narrow blocks and do not wrap convincingly around the outer arris; the butt end is a blank slab.
evidence.V4: Every stone, cap and plinth block carries the same ~0.06 stud chamfer that catches a highlight in the studio close-ups (end_x, quoins).
evidence.V5: Studio close-ups clean: no pinches, z-fighting or stray faceting; the dark V notches at the edge in quoins_flat are the designed mortar recesses between blocks.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light quoins/caps, mid field, dark plinth); colourways (brick, sandstone) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor white material, chamfered stone blocks, stone hue only - consistent with modular kit spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, pivot at grid corner; T1 tiling pass (iou 0.97).

artifacts: Small off-colour (cream/tan) sliver visible at the inner corner top in the three-quarter view, reads as an unintended strip rather than designed plaster
top_fixes: Make the quoins read as true alternating long/short stones wrapping both faces of the outer corner so the corner identity reads at 64 px
Break the rigid block grid with a few varied stone sizes / slight bevel offsets and add a small accent (e.g. a gold band or keystone) to give a small-scale tier
Resolve or colour-match the cream sliver at the inner top corner
